clue.text: People of the UK maybe in History and Geography, for example

definitions.meaning: citizens of a monarchy are the monarch's ...

explanation.surface: A school timetable listing British topics, or a census of Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both those owing allegiance to a crown and the areas of learning taught in school.

clue.text: Stated son needs help

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone announcing their boy requires assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Said is the past tense of say, so it means declared or stated.

clue.text: Some herbal titbits in cooked dish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few herb nibbles have gone into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in' as part of the definition; it is the link joining the hidden-word wordplay to the definition 'cooked dish'.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a wok-like pan, a Birmingham-born dish.

clue.text: Geology maybe has awfully nice teachers

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly treated and so rearranged

explanation.surface: The rocks lesson is taught by rather pleasant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Geology is one of the earth sciences, those studying the planet, so it is an example.

clue.text: Boy joins workers' organisation in US city

indicators.note: joins here means the boy is attached after the union abbreviation

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, Britain's federation of labour unions
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A lad signing up to a trade union in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the British Trades Union Congress; the boy comes after it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a large city in Arizona, in the American southwest.

clue.text: A public entertainment, not one a million miles away?

indicators.note: not tells us the following one is dropped from the entertainment word

parts.note: a fair is a funfair, an entertainment open to the public
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a show that feels very remote without someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'a million miles away' is a loose, exaggerated stand-in for great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a great distance is far off; a million miles away is a playful exaggeration of that.

clue.text: Appropriate procedure before buying a suit?

definitions.meaning: a tailor's ... is the trying on and adjusting of clothes

explanation.surface: Trying on clothes in a shop is the proper thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means suitable; the noun is the session where a garment is tried on and altered.

clue.text: Rebel in den, eager, properly prepared

indicators.note: properly prepared suggests the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A revolutionary hiding out in a hideaway, keen and well organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly prepared' rearranges DEN EAGER; 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or defies authority, much as a rebel does.

clue.text: Where oncoming traffic may be unseen? Crazy! (

definitions.text: Where oncoming traffic may be unseen?
definitions.meaning: literally, cars coming the other way are hidden ... of a road

explanation.surface: A driver's alarm at a blind corner.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being mad also literally describes the hidden stretch beyond a curve in the road.

clue.text: Indolent type I had left with hesitation

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, giving ID
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A lazy person confessing they hesitated before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones who avoids work is an idler, a noun for an indolent person.

clue.text: King Charles not favoured — no turning back — one in the soup?

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, the royal cipher of King Charles
someone out of favour is simply out

indicators.note: turning back says the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: A royal who has lost favour and cannot go back, ending up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' also means in trouble, fitting a disgraced king; but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried bread floated in soup, so it is one item in the soup.

clue.text: Like a soprano being pretentious?

definitions.meaning: a soprano's voice sounds high, read literally

explanation.surface: A singer accused of showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes inflated, grandiose language; read literally it describes a voice pitched up high.

clue.text: Horse in box pursued by crazy character

indicators.note: pursued by puts the crazy character after the box word

parts.note: a chest is a large box
a nut is a madman

explanation.surface: A horse in a horsebox, chased by a lunatic.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a reddish-brown horse, named for its coat colour.

clue.text: Old poet to run at back of house

indicators.note: at back of places the running word after the house abbreviation

parts.note: to run in a contest is to race

explanation.surface: An instruction to jog behind a home where a classical writer lived.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a Roman lyric poet of the first century BC, so an ancient versifier.

clue.text: Reclaim sports ground no longer operating?

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Trying to win back a playing field that has closed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park with playing fields.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something is to get it back, which is to reclaim it.

clue.text: Person who is holy and ancient presented in the theatre

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST
very old means aged

explanation.surface: An elderly saint putting on a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is staged when it is put on for an audience, a past participle like the definition.

clue.text: Girl's story about donkey

indicators.note: about says the fib goes around the animal

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A young woman's tale concerning a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' reads as Girl is, the 's linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassie is a Scots and northern English word for a young woman.

clue.text: Various sergeants etc. becoming spies

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the phrase taken in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Assorted army sergeants turning into undercover operatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges the twelve letters of SERGEANTS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret agents are covert operatives gathering intelligence, which is what spies do.

clue.text: Buried under storage container is a Japanese poem

indicators.note: in a down answer, buried under puts the a below the container

parts.note: a tank stores liquid or gas

explanation.surface: A verse from Japan concealed beneath a cistern.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanka is a classical five-line Japanese verse form, older than the haiku.

clue.text: The fellow sitting on road in a crowd

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on puts the fellow above the road

parts.note: the fellow is he

explanation.surface: A man sitting in the road amid a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals, and figuratively a mass of people.

clue.text: Recruits — small number having bad habits?

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
vices are wicked or harmful habits

explanation.surface: A handful of new recruits with unpleasant ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Habits are also nuns' robes, and novices are trainee nuns: a pun beneath the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are beginners newly taken in, as recruits are newcomers to a group.

clue.text: Eagle circling round one man

indicators.note: circling round says the bird word goes around the numeral

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A large bird of prey wheeling over a lone figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a male first name, and crosswords use man to signal any male name.

clue.text: Change of direction is a shock

definitions.meaning: a move to a new heading
a nasty ... is a fright or start

explanation.surface: Suddenly swerving gives the driver a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a rotation onto a new course and a sudden jolt of fright.

clue.text: It's said principal wouldn't allow adornment in hair

indicators.note: It's said marks that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a school principal is the head; something not allowed is banned

explanation.surface: A school head forbidding a pupil's hair accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A headband is a strip of fabric worn around the head, an ornament or hold for the hair.
